title: Credit Notes, Cancellation and Corrections
subtitle: The correction rules that decide whether your ledger and LHDN agree at year end
outcomes: Choose correctly between cancelling an e-Invoice and issuing a credit note
Reference original UUIDs on credit, debit and refund notes
Operate within the 72-hour window and the 300-character reason limit
Handle buyer rejection and active referencing documents without stalling the ledger
Design a written cancellation policy with named approvers and reason templates

slides.title: Two ways to undo, one right answer
bullets: Cancellation erases the document's validity and is only possible within 72 hours
A credit note preserves history: the original stays valid and the reduction is a new document
If money has moved, a refund note may also be needed alongside or after the credit note
The decision is driven by elapsed time and by whether a referencing note already exists
Write the decision rule down, because it will be made under pressure at 6pm on a Friday
slides.notes: Frame the choice as a rule, not a judgement call. Time first, then dependency. If it is inside 72 hours and nothing references the document, cancellation is clean. Otherwise the credit note is the compliant path, even if it feels heavier. The Friday-evening framing is deliberate: policy is what you rely on when nobody senior is available.

slides.title: Credit, debit and refund notes in ERPNext terms
bullets: A return against a Sales Invoice creates the ERPNext credit note, and the app submits it as type 02
Debit notes increase a sale and are usually created as a separate invoice with an explicit type
Refund notes accompany money returned to the buyer, not just a balance reduction
Every note needs a billing reference: the app reads the referenced invoice's stored UUID
The reference is mandatory: local validation refuses a note without it
slides.notes: Translate compliance into ERPNext muscle memory. Accounts staff already know how to create a return; what they do not know is that the app must find the original UUID to build the reference. That means the original invoice must have been submitted successfully. If the original was never validated, there is no UUID to reference and the correction needs a human decision.

slides.title: Making the cancellation call correctly
bullets: Cancellation sends a state change to LHDN with status cancelled and a mandatory reason
The reason is capped at 300 characters, so keep templates short and factual
Only documents validated within 72 hours can be cancelled; after that LHDN refuses
A cancellation is refused while a referencing credit or debit note is active
Cancelling the e-Invoice does not cancel the ERPNext invoice: decide both, in the right order

rows: Cancel or credit the note first

slides.notes: The three error names are worth memorising because they tell you exactly which rule you hit. OperationPeriodOver is a hard no. IncorrectState usually means somebody else already cancelled, or the status is stale. ActiveReferencingDocuments is the interesting one: it enforces the ordering rule that a correction must be unwound from the newest document backwards.

slides.title: Buyer rejection is a request, not a cancellation
bullets: A buyer rejecting a document in MyInvois puts it into a rejected state on their side
The supplier must still cancel it, because the supplier is the issuer
The client supports the reject verb for integrations that act for buyers
Rejection reasons should flow into your ticket system so the cause is fixed at source
Track rejections as a quality metric: they usually indicate a wrong buyer identity or amount
slides.notes: This confuses almost everyone the first time. A buyer cannot unilaterally remove a supplier's invoice from LHDN; they can request cancellation. If the request arrives after the 72-hour window, the answer is a credit note, and the buyer needs to hear that early. Recommend a short mailbox template for this conversation, because it happens under time pressure.

slides.title: Mirroring ERPNext cancellations safely
bullets: The setting Cancel e-Invoice when Sales Invoice is Cancelled is off by default, deliberately
When enabled, cancellation attempts are logged and never block the ERPNext cancellation
If the LHDN cancellation fails, you have a cancelled ledger document and a valid e-Invoice to fix by hand
Order matters: cancel the e-Invoice first, then the ERPNext invoice, when you control the sequence
Reconcile any exception the same day; a silent mismatch is worse than a failed attempt

callout.title: The half-cancelled state
callout.text: A cancelled Sales Invoice with a valid e-Invoice at LHDN is a real, common state. It needs a named person and a same-day fix, not a monthly cleanup.

slides.notes: Explain why the setting defaults to off: automatic mirroring sounds tidy but can produce half-cancelled states when LHDN refuses. Half-cancelled means the books say one thing and the tax platform says another, which is an audit finding. Either keep the setting off and cancel deliberately in both places, or turn it on with a daily exception review. Do not pretend the choice is free.

slides.title: Four common corrections and the compliant route
bullets: Wrong amount, inside 72 hours: cancel the e-Invoice, correct the invoice, submit the new version
Wrong amount, after 72 hours: credit note the difference, then invoice correctly if needed
Wrong buyer identity: cancel and reissue inside the window, otherwise credit and reissue
Goods returned in part: a return against the invoice producing a type 02 note for the returned quantity
Cancelled sale before delivery: cancel both the e-Invoice and the ERPNext invoice, then reconcile stock
slides.notes: Give people a lookup table rather than principles under stress. Each row names a situation and the compliant sequence. The goods-return case is the most common and the easiest: ERPNext already models it, so the only new skill is confirming the UUID reference was picked up. The cancelled-sale case adds a stock wrinkle, which is a reminder that e-Invoicing does not suspend inventory logic.

slides.title: The audit trail a cancellation leaves behind
bullets: The log stores the cancellation reason, the response and the time of the request
Keep the original request and response bodies, not just the final status
Reasons should be factual and reusable, for example duplicate submission or wrong billing entity
Review cancellations monthly by reason to find recurring process defects
Retention should match your statutory record-keeping obligations, agreed with finance
slides.notes: Auditors do not ask whether you cancelled documents; they ask why, how often and who approved. A reason field full of 'error' answers none of those questions. Show how a monthly pivot by reason turns a compliance obligation into a process improvement loop. This is also where the 300-character limit becomes a virtue: it forces brevity and reuse.

slides.title: Write the policy before go-live
bullets: Name who may cancel an e-Invoice: usually a finance lead plus one backup
Define the reason templates and forbid free text for the first three months
State when a credit note is mandatory, and who signs off on it
Set a response time for buyer rejection requests, measured in business hours
Review the policy after the first month, when you know which cases actually occur
slides.notes: Policy is the cheapest control you will ever write, and the least likely to exist. The 72-hour window makes response time a compliance variable, so a policy without an owner and a service level is decoration. Keep the document to one page: who, when, what wording, how fast, reviewed when.

lab.title: Cancel, correct and unwind in the right order
steps: Submit a clean invoice on sandbox and confirm the log reaches Valid with a UUID
Cancel the e-Invoice with a factual reason under 300 characters and confirm the cancelled state
Attempt the same cancellation again and read the IncorrectState error on the log
Submit a second invoice, then create a return against it and submit the type 02 credit note
Confirm the credit note's payload carries a BillingReference equal to the original UUID
Try to cancel the original invoice now and read the ActiveReferencingDocuments error
Cancel the credit note first, then cancel the original, and record the order in your runbook
Write the three reason templates your team will use, each under 300 characters
lab.done: Your log shows a cancellation, an IncorrectState refusal, an active-reference refusal and a successful unwind in the correct order, and the reasons are written for reuse rather than for today's incident.

quiz.question: An invoice was validated 80 hours ago and the price was wrong. What is compliant?
options: Cancel it, because the reason field allows late corrections
Issue a credit note referencing the original UUID
Edit the invoice and resubmit with the same number
Delete the invoice and create a new one
quiz.why: The 72-hour window has passed, so cancellation is refused by LHDN. A credit note carrying the original UUID is the correct correction.

quiz.question: What does ActiveReferencingDocuments mean when cancelling?
options: The invoice has unpaid installments
A credit or debit note referencing this document is still active
The customer has rejected the invoice
The submission UID has expired
quiz.why: LHDN refuses to cancel a document while a note references it, so you unwind from the newest document backwards.

quiz.question: A buyer rejects an e-Invoice. Who must cancel it?
options: The buyer, since they rejected it
The supplier, because they issued it
LHDN support
Nobody: rejection is final
quiz.why: Rejection is a request. The issuer must perform the cancellation, within the same 72-hour window, with a reason.

quiz.question: You enable mirroring of ERPNext cancellations. What operational risk do you accept?
options: Invoices will be submitted twice
A cancelled ERPNext invoice can be left with a valid e-Invoice if LHDN refuses the cancellation
Credit notes will be created automatically
Customers will be notified twice
quiz.why: Mirroring never blocks the ERPNext cancellation, so a refusal leaves a half-cancelled state that needs a same-day manual fix.

quiz.question: Which reason is best for a cancellation record?
options: Error
Wrong billing entity: reissued under ABC Sdn Bhd
Customer asked
Please cancel
quiz.why: Reasons should be factual, reusable and specific enough to survive an audit months later, within the 300-character limit.

narration: Chapter seven is corrections, where compliance meets accounting discipline. There are two ways to undo an e-Invoice. Cancellation erases the document and is only possible within seventy two hours of validation. A credit note preserves history: the original stays valid and the reduction becomes a new document that must reference the original UUID. The rule is time first, then dependency. Inside the window with nothing referencing the document, cancel. Otherwise, credit. In ERPNext a return against the invoice produces the type zero two credit note, and the app reads the referenced invoice's stored UUID. If the original was never validated, there is no UUID, and that needs a human decision. Three LHDN errors are worth memorising: operation period over means the window closed, incorrect state usually means it is already cancelled, and active referencing documents means a note still points at it, so you unwind from the newest backwards. Buyer rejection is not cancellation: the buyer requests it, the supplier performs it, and if the request arrives too late the answer is a credit note. Mirroring ERPNext cancellations defaults to off, deliberately, because a refused cancellation leaves a cancelled ledger document with a valid e-Invoice. Write the policy before go live: who may cancel, the reason templates, when a credit note is mandatory, and how fast you answer a buyer. In the lab you cancel, get refused, credit, and unwind.
